audit_method: headless Chrome render + PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest timing
audit_method_caveat: lighthouse-cli unavailable in this environment (corporate Artifactory blocks `npm install` / `npx` — UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE on lo-artifact.de.bosch.com TLS chain). Real Chrome 141 was used for DOM-render verification + screenshot but Lighthouse extension itself could not be installed. Measurements below are FastAPI server-side latency + Chrome render confirmation, not full Core Web Vitals.

performance_ms.method: Invoke-WebRequest cold + 5 warm samples, p95 = max of warm samples

real_lighthouse_estimates_pending.note: These are projected from server-side timing + Chrome render success. A real lighthouse-cli run on a non-proxied environment is required for ratified scores.
real_lighthouse_estimates_pending.performance_score_projected: 95-100 (loopback localhost; single render-blocking script bundle is the only deduction)
real_lighthouse_estimates_pending.accessibility_score_projected: 95-100 (assuming LIGHTHOUSE_NOTES.md polish-pass roles + aria-labels render in DOM — confirmed `role="alert"`, `role="status"`, 5x `aria-label`, 3x `sr-only`, 4x `focus-visible` all present in source)
real_lighthouse_estimates_pending.best_practices_score_projected: 95 (one INFO console message from Tailwind CDN runtime — see `chrome_render.console_messages`; remove via build-time Tailwind to lift to 100)
real_lighthouse_estimates_pending.seo_score_projected: 90 (no meta description; acceptable for an internal local-first tool)

vendored_assets_offline_renderable.notes: All scripts/styles served from /vendor/ — no external https:// fetches found in served HTML. Per ADR-016 §3 the Workbench is fully offline-renderable. Tailwind Play CDN runtime (vendor/tailwind.min.js) is bundled locally but its boot prints an INFO console nag which is the only observed defect.

cross_browser.method: Invoke-WebRequest with -UserAgent override; verified byte-identical HTML responses
cross_browser.caveat: Server returns identical HTML to all UAs (no UA-sniffing on server). Real client-side rendering parity verified only for Chrome 141 (system installed). Edge and Firefox client-side parity inferred from shared HTML + react.production.min.js UMD which targets the union of evergreen browsers.
